title: Elon Musk Backs 115K-Strong Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
summary: Elon Musk backs a 115K-signature petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO. Over 5,900 employees signed. What it means for AI builders and Nvidia's future.
body_markdown:
Nvidia Leadership Crisis


# Elon Musk Backs 115K-Strong Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO


By OpenTools Team


·


November 15, 2026


A petition demanding Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO has surpassed 115,000 signatures, with Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan among signatories. Over 5,900 current Nvidia employees have also signed, as the company's board faces mounting pressure from investors and staff alike.


## 115,000 Signatures and Counting


A petition demanding Jensen Huang's reinstatement as[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) CEO has gathered more than **115,000 signatures** as of Saturday afternoon, according to[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/elon-musk-other-tech-execs-sign-petition-calling-on-nvidia-to-reinstate-jensen-huang/) — including over 5,900 current Nvidia employees and 63,000 shareholders. The "Stand with Jensen" campaign, which launched after Huang's abrupt resignation on November 12, has become the most visible pushback against the board's decision to accept his departure before an internal investigation concluded.


The petition's organizers, who are not affiliated with Huang or Nvidia, argue the board removed him without "meaningful due process," per the petition's open letter reviewed by[Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/petition-reinstate-jensen-huang-nvidia-elon-musk-2026-11) , demands the board "bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts" and calls for disclosure of the investigation's scope, independence, and timeline. Signers include 5,248 current employees, 922 former employees, 53,233 shareholders, and 40,745 other supporters per the campaign's live tracker.


## Musk: 'Critical' Deals Are Handshakes With Jensen


Elon Musk publicly backed the petition on X, telling his 240 million followers: "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too." His reasoning goes beyond solidarity —[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/musk-says-nvidia-will-lose-critical-deals-without-jensen-huang-2026-11-14/) reported that Musk warned[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) would lose "critical" deals without Huang, noting many were "a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract."


Other prominent signatories,[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/elon-musk-other-tech-execs-sign-petition-calling-on-nvidia-to-reinstate-jensen-huang/) reports, include Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl. Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Barker wrote a separate letter to the board urging a "measured" approach to leadership succession, per[Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/petition-reinstate-jensen-huang-nvidia-elon-musk-2026-11) .


## Inside Nvidia, 'Bring Back THE Boss'


Internal dissent at[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) predates the public petition.[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/) reviewed internal communications showing a longtime engineer posted to the company's suggestion[box](https://opentools.ai/organizations/box) urging the board to weigh employee sentiment before acting. The post has drawn more than 1,600 comments, with one anonymous commenter writing: "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss."


Another employee sent a companywide email demanding transparency, writing: "I stand by Jensen. Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us," according to[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/) . About two dozen employees posted support on LinkedIn in the hours after Huang's resignation, while WIRED could not identify any public posts from Nvidia employees supporting his departure. One employee told[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/) : "Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen."


## The Scandal That Triggered the Fallout


Huang's resignation followed a cascade of revelations. He admitted to an extramarital affair with a Singapore-based tech executive whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect was recruited by China's top spy agency, per[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/musk-says-nvidia-will-lose-critical-deals-without-jensen-huang-2026-11-14/) .[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/) later reported additional affairs — one with a direct report and a third with another[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) employee, per Reuters. Huang wrote to employees admitting he was "unfaithful to \[his\] wife" and that there was "no excuse."


Nvidia's board announced an investigation into whether Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort," but accepted his resignation before the investigation concluded — a sequence that has frustrated employees and investors alike. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday that the Department of Justice had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy. The scandal has erased roughly **$1 trillion in market value** from Nvidia, per[WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/) .


## Investors Split as Board Stays Silent


The board, now chaired by former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones, has installed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while searching for a permanent successor. The board said it will consider both internal and external candidates but has not commented on the petition. Two notable investors — Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Barker of Atreides Management — wrote to the board Friday urging a "measured" approach, even if that means Huang returns, per[Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/petition-reinstate-jensen-huang-nvidia-elon-musk-2026-11) .


The petition site has acknowledged fake signatures — including "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and a misspelled reference to the Chinese leader — and organizers said they are "actively working" to remove them. But the core numbers remain staggering: 5,900+ current employees and 63,000+ shareholders represent a genuine groundswell that the board cannot easily dismiss.


## What This Means for AI Builders


For the AI developer ecosystem,[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) 's leadership crisis hits at the worst possible time. The company's GPUs power nearly every major AI training run, and its CUDA platform is the de facto standard for AI development. Any disruption to Nvidia's deal flow — especially the "handshake deals" Musk referenced, as[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/musk-says-nvidia-will-lose-critical-deals-without-jensen-huang-2026-11-14/) reported — could ripple through the supply of AI compute that startups and labs depend on.


The petition's signatory list reads like a who's-who of AI infrastructure stakeholders: Musk ([xAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/xai) , Tesla), Masad (Replit), Tan (Y Combinator), Sweeney (Epic Games). These are people whose companies run on Nvidia hardware. Their support isn't just personal loyalty — it's a bet that Huang's return is the fastest path back to stability in the AI chip supply chain. As one Nvidia employee told[Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/petition-reinstate-jensen-huang-nvidia-elon-musk-2026-11) , "Nvidia is not doomed without him, but it would not be the same."
